Swapping A and B is the most reported terminal-block mistake on installer forums. It isn't carelessness; it's a real conflict between specs. TIA/EIA-485-A defines "A" as the **negative** wire in the marking state and "B" as the positive. The Modbus 2002 spec and many vendor datasheets use the opposite convention; some vendors sidestep the issue with D+ and D- or D0 and D1 labels.

A multimeter settles the question before the first frame. With bias on the bus and no device transmitting, the wire with the higher DC voltage is B (D+). If A reads higher than B, the pair is swapped.

## Termination: 120 Ω at each end

Place a 120 Ω terminator at each physical end of the bus segment, never in between. That's the entire rule from the [Modbus over Serial Line Specification](https://www.modbus.org/docs/Modbus_over_serial_line_V1_02.pdf) , section 2.4.

Modbus RTU uses RS485 in half-duplex with 2 wires (A and B) plus an optional third wire for the signal common. Full-duplex 4-wire RS485 exists in the spec but isn't used by Modbus.

### What happens if you wire RS485 backwards?

The bus won't communicate and you'll see only CRC errors or no responses. No device is damaged by reversed polarity, so swap A and B and try again. This is a frequent issue because vendors label A and B inconsistently

3.4 Polarity Verification

RS-485 is polarity-sensitive. Many vendors label the non-inverting line as "A" or "D0" while others use "B" or "D1". A swapped pair does not damage equipment but causes the UART to see inverted data, producing CRC errors on every transaction. This is one of the two most common field errors (the other being baud rate mismatch).
Polarity test procedure:
1. Power down the master and slave.
2. Measure resistance between A and B at the master. Expect ~60 Ω if both terminations are present, ~120 Ω if only one end is terminated, or high-Z if neither end is terminated.
3. Power up the master only. With a voltmeter, measure the idle state voltage between A and B. A properly biased bus shows +200 mV to +1.5 V (B higher than A) when idle.
4. Compare with the slave's idle reading. If the slave shows the opposite polarity, swap the A/B pair at one end.
Some vendors (notably Modicon legacy documentation and a few Asian PLC platforms) use opposite A/B polarity from the TIA-485 standard.

How do I determine if my RS-485 bus has proper termination without an oscilloscope?

Power down all nodes and measure resistance between the A and B terminals at any node on the bus. With both ends terminated (120 Ω each, parallel = 60 Ω), the meter should read approximately 60 Ω. With one end terminated, 120 Ω. With no termination, high impedance (typically > 1 MΩ).
